All three work. Open http://maker:4001/manage.html — there's now a **Sort** control above the list, a **Delete** action on each item, and the **✎ edit** panel now includes the **link (URL)**.

**Please try:**

**1. Sorting.** Use the **Sort** dropdown (top-right of the list) and switch between **Newest saved**, **Oldest saved**, **Title A–Z**, and **Recently updated**. → I chose those four options with **Newest saved as the default**. Are those the sort orders you'd use, and is newest-first the right default? Any you'd add (e.g. by site)?

**2. Deleting — your call on the safety net.** Click **🗑 Delete** on any item. → It's removed immediately and a bar appears at the bottom: **"Deleted … — Undo"**, which restores it if you click within a few seconds. I chose an **undo bar** rather than a "Are you sure?" pop-up, so deleting stays quick but recoverable. Does the undo approach suit you, or would you prefer a confirmation prompt before deleting (or both)?

**3. Changing a saved URL — your call on re-fetching.** On any item click **✎ edit**; you'll now see a **Link (URL)** field and a checkbox **"Update title, description & preview from this link."** Change the URL (try `github.com`), tick the box, and press **Done** — the details refresh to match the new link. Leave the box unticked and the details stay as they were. → Is an **optional** refresh (your choice each time) right, or would you expect changing the URL to **always** refresh, or **never**?

Tell me your preferences on the delete safety net and the URL-refresh behavior especially.
